info.title: Bowmark API
info.description: Run real tasks on live websites over plain HTTP. Two calls: read the typed function library for your task with `GET /v1/library`, then send a short async JavaScript script written against it to `POST /v1/run`. Or call one site's functions directly: every site in `GET /v1/sites` has its own spec at `/v1/sites/{site}/openapi.json`. Guide: https://bowmark.ai/docs/api. Get a key at https://bowmark.ai/dashboard/keys.

get.summary: Read the function library for a task or a site
get.description: Read-only, touches no site, costs nothing. Returns the `bowmark.*` functions, their arguments and return types for the task. A query that matches nothing returns the index rather than an error. Markdown by default; send `Accept: application/json` for JSON.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: The task or the site's hostname (`flights`, `amazon.com`). Repeat it for a task with several parts (`?query=flights&query=hotels`), up to 6.

400.description: More than 6 queries in one request.

401.description: No API key, or a key that was refused.

post.summary: Run a script against the library on live sites
post.description: The script is the body of an async function: use `await` freely and `return` the result. It runs in a sandbox with the `bowmark` global and `log()`. Read `GET /v1/library` first for the exact function names.

egress.description: Optional. `link` sends every request of the run through your own Chrome (Bowmark Link) and fails with "Link not connected" when it is not open, never falling back to Bowmark's route. Any other value is a 400.

example.script: const { offers } = await bowmark.pcparts.search("RTX 5080"); return offers.slice(0, 3);

200.description: The run was accepted. That includes a script that threw (`status: error`) or paused for a sign-in (`status: needs_user`).

400.description: The body was malformed. `error` says what to send.

401.description: No API key, or a key that was refused.

402.description: The account is out of free usage, at its spend cap, or its card was declined. Fix billing at https://bowmark.ai/dashboard/billing.

429.description: Too many runs in flight on this account. Nothing was started or charged.

503.description: A failure on Bowmark's side. Retry.

post.summary: Save a script under a name
post.description: Saves a script you can later run by its id or name with `POST /v1/scripts/{ref}/run`. Saving over a name you already used replaces its script and keeps its id. The script is checked when you save it, so one that does not parse is refused here. Inside it, `input` is the object the run passes. Scripts belong to you, not to one key: every key on your account sees the same ones.

example.name: rintaro-slots
example.script: return await bowmark.providers.resy.checkAvailability({ venueId: input.venueId, date: input.date, partySize: 2 });

400.description: The body is not a script we can save (the reason is in `error`).

401.description: No API key, or a key that was refused.

parameters.description: The script's id or its name.

get.summary: List the sites you can call directly
get.description: Every site with its own functions. Each row carries `openapiUrl`, that site's own spec.

parameters.name: site
parameters.description: A site id from `GET /v1/sites` (`kayak`) or the site's host (`kayak.com`).

get.description: An OpenAPI 3.1 document with one operation per function of that site, each a `POST /v1/sites/{site}/{fn}`. Feed it to an SDK generator for a typed client.

404.description: No site by that id or host.

post.summary: Call one function of one site
post.description: The body is the function's arguments as an object keyed by parameter name. The site's own spec has the exact shape for each function. Same envelope, billing and status codes as `POST /v1/run`.

bearer.description: Your Bowmark API key (`bmk_…`), from https://bowmark.ai/dashboard/keys.

apiKeyHeader.name: X-Bowmark-Key
apiKeyHeader.description: The same key, for a client that cannot set `Authorization`.

RunEnvelope.description: What a run returns. `status` says whether the SCRIPT succeeded. A script that threw or paused for a login is still HTTP 200. Branch on `status`, not on the HTTP code.

runId.description: Stable id for this run. Quote it in a support or `report` message.

ok.description: False only when the run produced nothing usable.

status.description: `partial`: the result is real but some calls failed (see `incomplete`); `ok` stays true. `needs_user`: a person must sign in to a site first. Relay `meta.handoff.url` to them, then run again.

egress.description: The egress the run was given, present only when the request asked for one. `link`: every request went through the caller's own Chrome (Bowmark Link).

result.description: Whatever the script `return`ed. Any JSON value.

error.description: Why the run failed, in plain words. Null on success.

ms.description: How long the script itself ran, in milliseconds.

queuedMs.description: How long the run waited for a worker before starting. Present only when it was a second or more.

needs.description: The sign-ins this script is waiting on. Present when `status` is `needs_user`.

providerTitle.description: The site's name, to show a person.

incomplete.description: Present only when `status` is `partial`: which calls did not answer.

emptyHanded.description: Present when the script returned nothing while its calls returned rows, usually a filter that matched none of the site's own labels. Lists the label values the calls actually returned.

notes.description: Caveats a call attached to a complete answer. Never changes `status`.

handoff.description: A single-use sign-in link for a person to open. Expires at `expiresAt`.

concurrency.description: On a 429: how many runs are in flight and when to retry.

notice.description: Set when the account owner has not accepted the current Terms. Relay it to them.
